subject: Extraterrestrial life
hook: EXTRATERRESTRIAL LIFE IS NOT WHAT YOU THINK
angle: Extraterrestrial life could have technically emerged just 15 million years after the Big Bang, during a brief 'Habitable Epoch' when the universe's background temperature was between 0 and 100 degrees Celsius.
angle_support: During a period of about 7 million years, from about 10 to 17 million years after the Big Bang, the background temperature was between 373 and 273 K (100 and 0 °C; 212 and 32 °F), allowing the possibility of liquid water if any planets existed.
Avi Loeb (2014) speculated that primitive life might in principle have appeared during this window, which he called "the Habitable Epoch of the Early Universe".
title: When the Entire Universe Was Habitable
description: Long before the first modern solar systems formed, the newborn cosmos was bathed in mild temperatures. For a brief window shortly after the Big Bang, ambient heat allowed water to remain liquid across space without needing nearby stars.
narration: EXTRATERRESTRIAL LIFE IS NOT WHAT YOU THINK You picture alien worlds requiring eons around warm, mature stars. It was possible vastly earlier. Cosmic biology could have emerged when our universe was barely out of diapers. Around fifteen million years after cosmic birth, thermal radiation kept deep space between zero and a hundred degrees Celsius. In this brief epoch, liquid water could have pooled on any rocky surface, completely independent of stellar warmth. For several million years, the entire cosmos was a habitable zone.
